title: P02 tracers permit the 2013-2022 central Pacific AOU rise with fixed oxygen use and small age-weight changes
abstract: We test whether repeated P02 CFC-12, SF6 and oxygen means permit changed age distributions with a fixed oxygen-use law. At 28-32 N, 180-160 W, density 26.5 AOU rose 8.499 micromol/kg from 2013 to 2022. An exact continuous-age linear program matches both AOU means and each tracer within 5 percent. With a source oxygen budget of 300 micromol/kg and a fixed use rate of 4 micromol/kg/year, minimum total variation of age weights is 2.833 percent. This attains the sharp oxygen-budget bound. At a rate of 5, requiring every model component to retain 50 micromol/kg oxygen raises the minimum to 7.404 percent. Both scenarios fit all 199 spatial block resamples. With rate 5 and no component oxygen floor, one fixed rate fits all 15 regional density means, using separate spectra. A 100 micromol/kg floor raises the central 26.5 profile minimum to 24.803 percent. Three-degree bins give 2.599 and 8.508 percent. These results complement an earlier tracer-only fit with an unchanged spectrum: the tracer means do not distinguish steady transport with changed oxygen use from changed spectra with fixed use. The small minimum depends on oxygen-poor old components. The calculation does not establish a realizable circulation, estimate water replacement or attribute an outcrop contribution. Source saturation, uniform path use, sampling and an idealized oxygen budget limit inference. Code, exact-source provenance, aggregate results and positive witnesses are included.

display.caption: Central P02 AOU rise, minimum age-weight change across fixed use rates and oxygen bounds, and an example pair of positive age spectra. All tracer means have a 5 percent allowance.
